And now, I have subsetted for a particular list of genes that are in the R object plus column feature.name:

p2<-subset(p1,p1$V4 %in% plus$feature.name)

 

p2 is now an R object in my current workspace, visible after ls()

 

Now I want to read.transcript.features of p2:

p3<-read.transcript.features("p2",up.flank=500,down.flank=100)

 

I get an error:

Error in file(con, "r") : cannot open the connection
In addition: Warning message:
In file(con, "r") : cannot open file 'p2': No such file or directory

 

Because the command thinks p2 is in the getwd().
The documentation assumes that the bedfile is external in the getwd().  What is the correct command to read.transcript.features when the bed file is an R object in my current workspace (ls())?

 

Thanks,

Michelle

messages.author: e4181d5c40fc094c
messages.subject: Re: [methylkit_discussion] read.transcript.features when BED file is an object
parts:
One possible way is
  • Write down the subset p2 as a bed file (rtracklayer package will help you in exporting dataframe to bed file)
  • read the bed file back into methylKit using read.transcript.features

Other possible way is to subset a transcript features file read in methylkit (not sure if this works, but I would try to check)

  • read a bed file using read.transcript.features
  • read the list of genes/transcript names as a vector/dataframe.
  • filter like this 
    P.obj[P.obj$exons$name==plus], where P.obj is an object obtained from read.transcript.features and plus is a df (of interested genes/transcript names)

Regards,
Kalyan
